reasons.claim: The chain is three links joined by «عن», ending at the Imam who speaks, as both readers read it.
reasons.quote: رَوَى عَاصِمُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ

reasons.claim: The first level holds a named shaykh and an unnamed group as co-transmitters.
reasons.quote: عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُوسَى بْنِ بَابَوَيْهِ وَ جَمَاعَةٌ

reasons.claim: The chain runs to Abu al-Samit, who heard the Imam named after the chain, the last link.
reasons.quote: عَنْ أَبِي الصَّامِتِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (ع)

reasons.claim: One transmitter and the Imam he relates from; the readers read exactly this.
reasons.quote: وَ رَوَى دَاوُدُ بْنُ سِرْحَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ

reviews.question: the author of a cited book / a source known only by a title («نوادر الحكمة»): whether the book's author is a link

reasons.claim: The report cites a book by title and then the Imam's saying; no transmitter is written, so the Imam is the only link.
reasons.quote: وَ فِي نَوَادِرِ اَلْحِكْمَةِ أَنَّ اَلصَّادِقَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ

reasons.claim: If the owner rules the cited book's author a link, an unnamed link would stand before the Imam; the Imam stays last either way.

reviews.uncertainty_note: The unruled question about a cited book could add a link before the Imam.

reasons.claim: The gap «عمن أخبره» stands between Hammad and Hariz in the text's order, then the Imam.
reasons.quote: رَوَى حَمَّادُ بْنُ عِيسَى عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ

reasons.claim: Al-Zuhri narrates an encounter in which the Imam speaks; the speaker is the last link (ruling 9).
reasons.quote: رُوِيَ عَنِ اَلزُّهْرِيِّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ قَالَ لِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ

reasons.claim: The Prophet quoted inside the Imam's words is not a link (ruling 5).
reasons.quote: وَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ

reasons.claim: Ibn Abi Umayr relates from Ibn Udhayna; Zurara is only addressed and is not a link (ruling 4).
reasons.quote: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ قَالَ قَالَ اِبْنُ أُذَيْنَةَ قُلْتُ لِزُرَارَةَ

reasons.claim: Ibn Udhayna heard two co-transmitters relating from the Imam, giving two routes.
reasons.quote: سَمِعْتُ مُحَمَّدَ بْنَ مُسْلِمٍ وَ بُكَيْراً يَرْوِيَانِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ

reviews.question: a first-person narrative with an unnamed speaker or implicit transmission: the report opens «قال: وسألت» continuing an earlier report whose chain is not in the packet, so the asker and the chain before him cannot be read

reasons.claim: The report opens with «قال» and a first-person asker who is not named; by ruling 7 it inherits from an earlier report, but no previous report is given.
The Imam asked is the last link either way, but the reading drops the asker and the inherited chain, so the shown chain may be incomplete.

reviews.uncertainty_note: The inherited chain and the asker's identity are not in the packet.

reasons.claim: Two co-transmitters at the second level, then their fathers as a relation link.
reasons.quote: عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبَوَيْهِمَا

reasons.claim: The chain continues through relations to Amir al-Mu'minin, who relays the Prophet, who is not a link.
reasons.quote: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَنْ أَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

reviews.question: the Prophet speaking a one-sentence report with no transmitter (here not even named in the text)

reasons.claim: The report is a bare saying with no transmitter before it; the readers rightly give no routes.
